## New term request: microfold cell of palatine tonsil

**Proposed label:** microfold cell of palatine tonsil

**Definition:** A microfold cell that is part of the epithelium of the palatine tonsil, a nasopharynx-associated / Waldeyer's-ring mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue. It is specialized for transcytosis of luminal antigen across the tonsil crypt (reticulated) lymphoepithelium to underlying lymphoid tissue, expressing the conserved microfold-cell program (SPIB, SOX8, GP2, MARCKSL1). It is a distinct antigen-transporting cell type co-resident with, but separate from, the crypt reticulated epithelial cell. In current tonsil single-cell atlases it is under-resolved (M-cell markers appear scattered within the 'crypt cell' cluster), whereas in the adenoid (a related Waldeyer's-ring MALT) it is resolved as distinct immature and mature microfold-cell clusters.

**Parent (is_a):** epithelial cell (CL:0000066)

**Anatomical location:** tonsil epithelium (UBERON:0013696)

**Logical axioms:**
- `part of` (BFO:0000050) some **tonsil epithelium** (UBERON:0013696) — Resides in the crypt (reticulated) epithelium of the palatine tonsil.
- `capable of` (RO:0002215) some **transcytosis** (GO:0045056) — Transcytoses luminal antigen across the tonsil crypt epithelium.
- `capable of part of` (RO:0002216) some **mucosal immune response** (GO:0002385) — Delivers antigen to sub-epithelial lymphoid tissue, initiating mucosal immunity.

**Synonyms:**
- M cell of palatine tonsil (exact)
- tonsil microfold cell (exact)
- Waldeyer's ring M cell (related)

**References:**
- Alvarez-Arguedas et al. (2025). DOI: 10.1016/j.mucimm.2025.07.006 ; PMID:40721095 — Human adenoid (NALT, Waldeyer's ring) M cells resolved as distinct immature/mature clusters; share a common gene set with palatine-tonsil M cells and gut/airway M cells.
- Massoni-Badosa et al. (2024). DOI: 10.1016/j.immuni.2024.01.006 ; PMID:38301653 — Human tonsil atlas: M-cell markers (SPIB, MARCKSL1) detected within 'crypt' epithelial cells but no discrete M-cell cluster annotated (under-resolved).
- Kimura et al. (2019). DOI: 10.1084/jem.20181604 ; PMID:30877171 — Conserved SOX8-dependent M-cell maturation program.
- Han (2024). DOI: 10.1165/rcmb.2024-0002ED ; PMID:38301262 — Cross-MALT conservation of the M-cell program (gut/airway).

**Justification:** Intended DIRECT PARENT is the proposed general 'microfold cell' term (companion NTR #3684); parent is set provisionally to epithelial cell (CL:0000066) here because the general term does not yet exist. M cells of the palatine tonsil are long established by ultrastructure/immunohistology and share the conserved M-cell program; they are under-resolved in current tonsil scRNA atlases (markers within 'crypt cells') but resolved in the adenoid. This is a DISTINCT cell type co-resident in the crypt reticulated epithelium — NOT a subtype of the crypt epithelial cell (see companion crypt NTR). Species-neutral. GP2/SPIB/SOX8/MARCKSL1 kept textual.
